description:
fz-5xp.15 asked for String.Chars with Elixir's five builtin impls. Four landed:
Atom (with the `nil -> ""` case), Binary, Integer, Float. LIST DID NOT.

    to_string([1, 2])
      elixir -> <<1, 2>>      the list is a charlist of codepoints
      fz     -> no impl

`String.Chars.List` is `List.to_string/1`, which is charlist-to-binary
conversion, and Elixir's version is iodata-shaped rather than a flat map:

    List.to_string([0x64, "ee", [~c"p"]])   # => "deep"

nested lists and embedded binaries included.

WHY IT WAS LEFT OUT rather than half-built: charlists are deferred across this
project (see the fz-g58 enum epic, which excludes them deliberately). Adding a
codepoints-only `List.to_string` would introduce a partial charlist notion in
one protocol impl while the rest of the library has none, and the partial
version would answer `[0x64, "ee"]` with a panic where Elixir answers "dee" --
a shape people actually write.

NOT ON THE GOAL PROGRAM'S PATH. `Json.encode` renders a list structurally as
`[...]`, never through `to_string`, and interpolating a charlist is not
something the decoder or encoder does. So this does not block fz-5xp.17.

DONE = either charlists arrive and `String.Chars.List` is `List.to_string/1`
in full, or fz decides it has no charlists and the impl is deliberately absent
with that written down where a reader will find it. Both are defensible; the
current state -- silently missing one of five -- is not.

Blocked behind whatever settles charlists.

comments.text:
AUTHORIZED to stay as it is for now (user, 2026-09-07: 'we're in a better
position for now'). The absent String.Chars.List impl is a knowingly accepted
gap, not an oversight, and this ticket is the record of it.

title: String.Chars has four of Elixir's five impls: List is absent
